_README: The Tier 1 blocking core. One recorded decision per term in profanity_wordlists.json: `tier1: true` means Tier 1 may reject a message containing it BEFORE it is sent; `tier1: false` means the term is Tier 2's only, judged by the LLM with the message in front of it. The default for a new or unclassified term is Tier 2 - a term reaches Tier 1 only by carrying a reason here, and tests/test_moderation_tier1_terms.py refuses to load a wordlist term that has no entry at all.

_policy.promotion_rule: Evidence-POSITIVE. A term reaches Tier 1 only with a `review` record whose basis is one of: `not_a_word_in_any_orthography` (the needle contains a digit, so it can only match a deliberately obfuscated spelling), `curator_attested` (English, checked by a native English speaker for an ordinary English sense), or `native_review` (a named native speaker and date - there are none yet, which is why 29 languages have no plain-word terms in Tier 1). Absence of a collision is NOT evidence: three rounds of adversarial review found `faggot` (a British dish), `hoer` (one who hoes), Greek `kariola` (a bed), Turkish `kaltak` (a saddle frame), Portuguese `viado` (striped fabric), Korean `byeongsin` (the year 丙申) and `Chuj` (a Mayan language) among terms that scored zero everywhere the gate could look. Adding a language to Tier 1 is a review task, not a code change.
_policy.decision_rule: A term is universal when no supported language has a benign homograph of the surface form Tier 1 matches. `collisions` records every language where wordfreq measures the form at or above the threshold for that language's list size; each one must then carry an `adjudication` of no_benign_sense, or the term stays Tier 2.
_policy.frequency_is_a_tripwire_not_a_decider: wordfreq measures how often a form is written, not whether it is benign. `fuck` scores 4.85 in Danish and 4.29 in German because the swear is borrowed, not because it is innocent there, so automatic demotion on a high score would strip the most universal terms out of Tier 1. The gate is one-directional: a high score forces a recorded adjudication; a low score approves nothing. Absence of a score proves nothing either - zipf_frequency('pica', 'sk') is 0.0 for the one collision the instructions doc had already named.
_policy.length_floor: 4 characters for Latin-script needles, 3 for other alphabets and abugidas, 2 for Hangul, kana and ideographs. Below that, a needle is an ordinary word somewhere among thirty languages and exact matching does not save it.
_policy.matching: Casefold, drop invisible characters, NFC, collapse runs of three or more identical characters. Whole-token equality; no diacritic stripping, no leetspeak or homoglyph folding, no prefix matching, and no language identification of any kind.
_policy.review_status: The wordlist and these decisions were LLM-generated and curated by one non-native curator. NO NATIVE SPEAKER HAS REVIEWED ANY LANGUAGE. The frequency gate sees only what a frequency list can see: it is blind to register, regional sense, reclaimed usage, and to every language wordfreq does not carry. Treat `no_collision_measured` as 'nothing objected', not as 'verified safe'.
_policy.what_demotes_a_term: ANY recorded benign reading of the surface form Tier 1 matches demotes the term, whatever kind of word it is: an ordinary common noun (`faggot`, a British dish; `pica`, a typographic unit), a proper noun (`Fucking`, an Austrian village until 2021), or a case-sensitive technical identifier that casefolding merges with the term (`fucK`, the gene symbol for L-fuculokinase, NCBI gene 946022). An earlier revision exempted the last two and recorded them on the term as accepted pre-send false positives instead. That contradicted the decision rule in this same file and it was a gate softening: `The fucK gene encodes L-fuculokinase.` and `The Austrian village of Fucking was renamed Fugging in 2021.` both returned M_FORBIDDEN. The exemption is gone, the key that carried it is gone, and tests/test_moderation_tier1_terms.py fails on any entry that reintroduces either. Tier 1 is smaller for it, which is the trade D1 already makes: a demoted term is judged by Tier 2 with the message in front of it.
